stem: The angle $\theta$ is acute and $\{=f1}\theta=\frac{\{=WCMD[v1]}{{=NUM[v1]}}}{\{=DCMD[v1]}{{=DEN[v1]}}}$. Without a calculator, which of the following is the value of $\{=f2}\theta$?
solution: List the values of $\{=f1}$ at the special angles, from the triangle with sides $1$, $1$, $\sqrt{2}$ and the triangle with sides $1$, $2$, $\sqrt{3}$: $\{=f1}30^{\circ}=\frac{\{=WCMD[c0]}{{=NUM[c0]}}}{\{=DCMD[c0]}{{=DEN[c0]}}}$, $\{=f1}45^{\circ}=\frac{\{=WCMD[c1]}{{=NUM[c1]}}}{\{=DCMD[c1]}{{=DEN[c1]}}}$ and $\{=f1}60^{\circ}=\frac{\{=WCMD[c2]}{{=NUM[c2]}}}{\{=DCMD[c2]}{{=DEN[c2]}}}$.
The given value $\frac{\{=WCMD[v1]}{{=NUM[v1]}}}{\{=DCMD[v1]}{{=DEN[v1]}}}$ matches only $\{=f1}{=ang}^{\circ}$, so $\theta={=ang}^{\circ}$.
Now find the ratio that was asked for at this angle: $\{=f2}\theta=\{=f2}{=ang}^{\circ}=\frac{\{=WCMD[v2]}{{=NUM[v2]}}}{\{=DCMD[v2]}{{=DEN[v2]}}}$.

So $\{=f2}\theta=\frac{\{=WCMD[v2]}{{=NUM[v2]}}}{\{=DCMD[v2]}{{=DEN[v2]}}}$. The value $\frac{\{=WCMD[v1]}{{=NUM[v1]}}}{\{=DCMD[v1]}{{=DEN[v1]}}}$ belongs to $\{=f1}\theta$, so it is not the value of $\{=f2}\theta$.
notes: ADVANCED gap. A two-step recall of the special-angle table, in the book's own option style (ex5-3-1, values written as a fraction N over D, so tan 45 is 1 over 1 and tan 60 is root 3 over 1, exactly as the book prints them). The student is told an acute angle theta has one ratio equal to a table value, must recognise which special angle that is (30 or 60), then state a DIFFERENT ratio of the same angle. Only the book's special triangles (1,1,root2 and 1,2,root3) are used; no equation solving, no expression evaluation, no calculator. Every instance is exact: 12 distinct instances (3 given ratios x 2 asked ratios x angles 30 or 60), each with a unique special angle because sin, cos and tan are one-to-one on the acute angles. Distractor slots have fixed meanings so the misconception ids are always true: (1) the GIVEN value repeated and (2) the THIRD ratio's value, both mc wrong-ratio-same-angle; (3) the ratio asked, but read at 45 degrees, mc wrong-triangle-for-angle; (4) the correct value upside down (1/2 -> 2/1, root3/2 -> 2/root3, 1/root3 <-> root3/1), mc ratio-upside-down. The generator constraints enforce that all five options are distinct, and I checked all 12 combinations numerically (correct value, uniqueness of the angle, five distinct values and five distinct decimals). Deliberately NOT included: 45 degrees as the base angle, because sin 45 = cos 45 makes the given value or the third ratio coincide with the answer and the four fixed distractor slots collapse; 45 degrees is still tested as the wrong-triangle distractor. Also NOT included: a decimal distractor for mc calculator-decimal-not-surd, because a decimal such as 0.87 is approximately the right value and a careful solver could defend it, which makes the key ambiguous. TEMPLATE NOTE for the reviewer: every value is printed as \frac{N}{D}. The command name is supplied by a hole (\sqrt or \mathrm) so one template can print every value; \mathrm{2} wraps a plain digit and renders identically to a bare 2. Choice texts carry no dollar signs, like the book's own choices; the stem and solution steps do.
